claims.text: The baseline material is nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution nanoparticles dispersed on conventional carbon black.
The controlled intervention is replacement of conventional carbon black with nitrogen-doped carbon.
Nitrogen-doped carbon creates interfacial electronic interactions with supported metal nanoparticles.
Nitrogen dopants alter the electronic properties of the carbon support.
The nitrogen-doped support causes interfacial charge transfer between the support and PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles.
Interfacial charge transfer shifts the d-band center of surface atoms in the PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles.
The electronic modification tunes the binding strengths of ethanol and key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Adjusted adsorption energies lower activation barriers for ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Nitrogen-induced metal-support interactions can suppress nanoparticle sintering or metal redispersion-related degradation.
Nitrogen-induced electronic or coordination effects can suppress metal dissolution or oxidation.
Relative to conventional carbon, nitrogen-doped carbon will increase ethanol-oxidation current density and turnover frequency.
Relative to conventional carbon, nitrogen-doped carbon will slow performance decay during extended potential cycling.
In situ XAS or UPS will reveal a significant d-band-center shift in the nitrogen-doped-carbon-supported catalyst.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold at room temperature in 0.5 M KOH.
The behavior may differ at other temperatures or in highly acidic electrolytes.
Interfacial electronic and coordination effects from nitrogen are documented in other supported metal or high-entropy-alloy systems.
The quantitative relationship between a d-band-center shift and catalytic enhancement in complex multimetal solid solutions is uncertain.
